info.title: SafeRoute API
info.description: SafeRoute is a personal-safety navigation API. Safety information is context, never a guarantee that a route or area is safe. SafeRoute is not an emergency service; in an emergency call your local emergency number (112 in India).

tags.name: operational
tags.description: Unversioned probes for the platform (liveness, readiness). Not for app features.

tags.name: me
tags.description: The signed-in user's own account and consents. Every operation needs a Firebase ID token (phone sign-in).

tags.name: search
tags.description: Place search through a geocoding provider. Queries are rate-limited and are not stored or logged.

tags.name: routing
tags.description: Walking and driving routes between two points, computed from OpenStreetMap data. Origins, destinations and routes are not stored or logged. A route is a way to travel, never a statement that it is safe.

tags.name: contacts
tags.description: The signed-in user's emergency contacts (up to 5). Needs the `sos_alerts` consent. The server never sends a message to a contact: the user sends each invite from their own phone. Names, numbers and opt-out tokens never travel in a URL and are not logged.

tags.name: public
tags.description: Public by design, no sign-in: the page and the call with which an emergency contact, who has no account, opts out.

RequestId.description: Correlation ID for this request. Echoes a well-formed incoming `X-Request-Id` (8–64 characters of `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ -`), otherwise a fresh UUID.

CacheControlNoStore.description: Always `no-store`: the response must never be cached.

WwwAuthenticate.description: Always `Bearer`: send a Firebase ID token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds to wait before trying again. Present when the server knows how long (a rate limit); absent otherwise.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials (`unauthorized`). Refresh the ID token and retry once.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed: `forbidden`, `bootstrap_required`, `account_deleted`, `consent_required` or `adult_required`. Final: retrying the same request does not help.

NotFound.description: No such route or resource (`not_found`), or no way between two places (`no_route_found`).

Gone.description: The resource existed but has expired or ended (`gone`).

UnprocessableContent.description: The input is well-formed but cannot be served: `outside_covered_area`, `route_too_long` or `location_not_routable`. Final for this input: change it instead of retrying.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded (`rate_limited`). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds when it is sent.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency is unavailable (e.g. `db_unavailable`, `db_not_configured`, `auth_unavailable`, `auth_not_configured`, `search_unavailable`, `search_not_configured`, `routing_unavailable`, `routing_not_configured`). Retry with backoff, or after `Retry-After` when it is sent.

firebaseBearer.description: Firebase ID token from phone sign-in, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. 401 → refresh the token and retry once; 503 `auth_unavailable` → retry with backoff.

type.description: Problem type URI. `about:blank` means `title` is the HTTP status phrase.

detail.description: Human-readable, generic explanation. Never contains personal data.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code; clients switch on this, not on `title` or `detail`. Open set: clients must tolerate unknown values. Currently defined: `validation_error`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `bootstrap_required`, `account_deleted`, `consent_required`, `adult_required`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `phone_already_registered`, `account_deletion_required`, `invalid_contact`, `contact_exists`, `contact_opted_out`, `contact_limit_reached`, `gone`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error`, `db_unavailable`, `db_not_configured`, `auth_unavailable`, `auth_not_configured`, `search_unavailable`, `search_not_configured`, `outside_covered_area`, `route_too_long`, `location_not_routable`, `no_route_found`, `routing_unavailable`, `routing_not_configured`, `http_error`.

requestId.description: Same value as the `X-Request-Id` response header; quote it in bug reports.

errors.description: Present for `validation_error`: one entry per invalid input.

ProblemDetails.description: Error body for every 4xx/5xx response (media type `application/problem+json`).

path.description: Location of the invalid input, e.g. `body.contacts.0.name` or `query.limit`.

code.description: Why it is invalid (e.g. `invalid_type`, `too_small`). Open set.

ValidationIssue.description: One invalid input. Never contains the submitted value.

IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated key (e.g. a UUID) for a retryable state-changing call. The server stores key → response for 24 h and replays the stored response for a repeat (Plan v7 §6.2).

version.description: Deployed build version of the service (not the contract version).

checks.description: One entry per dependency this instance needs to serve traffic.

phoneE164.description: Verified phone number in E.164 form, from the sign-in token.

locale.description: UI language: `en` or `bn`. Clients must tolerate unknown values.

role.description: `user`, `moderator` or `admin`. Clients must tolerate unknown values.

locale.description: UI language for the new account. Default `en`. Ignored if it already exists.

displayName.description: Name shown to the user's emergency contacts. Trimmed; 1–80 characters; no control characters. Ignored if the account already exists.

BootstrapMeRequest.description: Settings and consent for a new account. `consent` is needed to create an account (optional in the schema only because an existing account does not need it). The phone number is never sent: the server takes it from the verified ID token. Unknown properties are ignored.

ageConfirmed.description: True when the user declared "I am 18 or older". Anything else → 403 `adult_required`. No date of birth is collected.

noticeVersion.description: Version of the consent notice the user was shown.

noticeLocale.description: Language the notice was shown in.

items.description: What the consent is for. Open set; currently accepted: `account_core`, `sos_alerts`, `live_sharing`, `safety_reports`.

purposes.description: Purposes the user agreed to. Must contain `account_core`.

BootstrapConsent.description: The age declaration and the consent the user gave on the onboarding notice. Needed to create an account; ignored when the account already exists.

items.description: One entry per purpose the user has ever decided on, ordered by purpose.

purpose.description: What the consent is for. Clients must tolerate unknown values.

status.description: `granted` or `withdrawn`. Clients must tolerate unknown values.

noticeVersion.description: Version of the notice this decision was made under.

decidedAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the decision.

Consent.description: The user's latest decision for one purpose.

noticeVersion.description: Version of the consent notice the user was shown.

noticeLocale.description: Language the notice was shown in.

SetConsentRequest.description: The user's decision for the purpose in the path.

maxContacts.description: How many contacts a user can have.

invitedAt.description: When the user confirmed that they sent the invite SMS from their own phone; null until then. The server sends no message.

optedOutAt.description: When the contact opted out through the public page; null otherwise. An opted-out contact must never be alerted and cannot be invited again.

Contact.description: One emergency contact of the signed-in user.

name.description: What the user calls this contact: 1 to 80 characters after trimming, no control characters.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 form: `+`, country code, number, digits only (7 to 15 digits).

name.description: What the user calls this contact: 1 to 80 characters after trimming, no control characters.

RenameContactRequest.description: The new name of the contact.

optOutToken.description: A new opt-out token for this contact, returned once and never stored in plaintext. The app puts it in the FRAGMENT of the opt-out link (`<API address>/c#<token>`) inside the SMS the user sends. Keep it in memory only: never log or save it.

ContactInvite.description: What the app needs to build an invite SMS.

ContactOptOutResult.description: The contact is opted out. Says nothing about the contact or who added them.

token.description: The token from the fragment of the opt-out link.

results.description: A name search: places near the requested point first, then places from further away; within each group, best match first. A search by kind or brand: nearest first, all inside the circle. Empty when nothing was found.

attribution.description: Credit line the app must show next to the results when it is not null (required by the terms of the geocoding provider and of the map data).

searchedRadiusKm.description: Present for a search by kind or brand around a point: the radius, in kilometres, of the circle that was searched. The first circle is widened once when it holds too few places, never beyond 25 km. Every result lies inside it, and nothing outside it was looked at.

searchedAround.description: Present together with `searchedRadiusKm`: what the centre of the circle was. `near`: the point of the request. `placeHint`: a place named in `q` ("pharmacy near Exampletown"); `distanceMeters` is then measured from that place, not from the point of the request. Open set.

id.description: Opaque identifier from the geocoding provider. Do not parse or store it.

label.description: Longer text that places the name (area, district, state). May be empty.

kind.description: Kind of place. Open set: clients must tolerate unknown values.

distanceMeters.description: Straight-line distance in metres from the rounded `nearLatitude`/`nearLongitude` of the request to this place, rounded to 100 m. Present only when the request carried that point. It is measured from the rounded point, so it is approximate: about 1 km either way.

matchType.description: Why the place is in the list: `name` (its name matched the text), `category` (it is of the kind asked for) or `brand` (it is of that kind and carries the name of the brand). Sent with every result since 0.8.0. Open set: clients must tolerate unknown values. It says nothing about the quality or safety of a place.

q.description: What the user typed. Required unless `category` is sent. A word for a kind of place, or a well-known brand, is searched as that kind or brand (see the operation). After trimming, collapsing whitespace and Unicode NFC normalisation it must be 2 to 100 Unicode code points with no control characters. Any script is accepted.

nearLatitude.description: Latitude of the area to prefer, WGS84 decimal degrees; send it together with `nearLongitude` or not at all. Places near it come first; places further away follow when too few are near. The server rounds it to two decimals (about 1 km) before using it; send a coarse point (the map centre, or a position already rounded to two decimals), never a precise position.

nearLongitude.description: Longitude of the area to prefer; see `nearLatitude`.

language.description: Preferred language of the result names.

category.description: A kind of place to look for near the point, for a quick-search button. When it is sent, `q` may be left out and is ignored. Open set: the values this version knows are bank, atm, pharmacy, hospital, clinic, fuel, restaurant, grocery, bus, train, public_transport, police, post_office, school, college; an unknown value is a 400. Send the point with it: without `nearLatitude`/`nearLongitude` there is no circle to search, and the answer is a plain name search for the word.

SearchRequest.description: A place search: `q`, `category` or both. Sent as a request body so that the text and the area never appear in a URL.

routes.description: Fastest first, then up to two alternatives.

attribution.description: Credit line the app must show with the routes (required by the map data).

id.description: Opaque identifier of this route within this response, for selecting it in the app. It means nothing to the server afterwards: routes are not stored.

durationSeconds.description: Estimated travel time without traffic. An estimate, not a promise.

encoding.description: Encoded polyline with six decimals: latitude then longitude, as differences.

geometry.description: The whole line of the route.

bbox.description: Box around the route: [minLongitude, minLatitude, maxLongitude, maxLatitude].

Route.description: One way to travel between the two points. Says nothing about safety.

mode.description: How the person travels. Driving means a car on roads open to cars.

departAt.description: When the trip starts, RFC 3339 with an offset. Validated and otherwise ignored for now: routes do not depend on the time of day yet.

RouteRequest.description: A request for routes between two points. Sent as a request body so that no position ever appears in a URL. The two points must be at least 20 m apart.

IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated key (e.g. a UUID) for a retryable state-changing call. The server stores key → response for 24 h and replays the stored response for a repeat (Plan v7 §6.2).
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description: Answers "is this process up and serving HTTP?". Does no I/O (no database, no provider), so a slow dependency never makes the platform restart a healthy instance.
Answers "can this instance serve traffic that needs the database?". Returns 503 (`db_unavailable` or `db_not_configured`) when it cannot. Never includes connection details.

200.description: The instance and its database are ready.

post.summary: Create the signed-in user's account if needed
post.description: Call after every sign-in. Creates the account for the token's Firebase user (201) or returns the existing one unchanged (200); safe to retry. The phone number comes from the verified token, never from the body. Creating an account needs `consent` from the onboarding notice: without it → `consent_required` (403); without `ageConfirmed: true` → `adult_required` (403); in both cases nothing is stored. For an existing account `consent` is ignored. Other errors: `phone_already_registered` (409) when another account holds the number, `account_deleted` (403).

200.description: The account already existed; returned unchanged.

get.description: The latest decision for each purpose the user has decided on. A purpose that was never asked is absent; treat it as not granted.

put.summary: Grant or withdraw consent for one purpose
put.description: Records the decision and returns the latest state; safe to retry. Ask just-in-time, when the feature that needs the purpose is first used. Errors: `validation_error` (400) for an unknown purpose; `account_deletion_required` (409) when withdrawing `account_core`, which can only be withdrawn by deleting the account. **Withdrawing `sos_alerts` deletes all of the user's emergency contacts**, and their opt-out links stop working, in the same step; it cannot be undone.

schema.description: What the consent is for. Open set; currently accepted: `account_core`, `sos_alerts`, `live_sharing`, `safety_reports`.

parameters.description: What the consent is for. Open set; currently accepted: `account_core`, `sos_alerts`, `live_sharing`, `safety_reports`.
parameters.name: purpose

200.description: The latest decision for this purpose.

get.summary: List the signed-in user's emergency contacts
get.description: The server is the source of truth; the app keeps a copy for use without a network. Removed contacts are not listed. Opted-out contacts are listed with `optedOutAt` set and must never be alerted.

post.description: Adds a contact, up to 5 per user. Needs the `sos_alerts` consent: the latest decision must be `granted`, otherwise 403 `consent_required` and nothing is stored. The server sends no message to a contact: no SMS, push or call. Errors (409): `invalid_contact` (the user's own number), `contact_exists` (already a contact), `contact_opted_out` (this number opted out and cannot be added again), `contact_limit_reached`. No `Idempotency-Key`: a number can be added only once, so a retry that reached the server the first time gets `contact_exists`; read the list again and continue. `rate_limited` (429) carries `Retry-After`.

patch.description: Changes the name only; the number cannot be changed (remove the contact and add it again). Another user's contact, or a removed one, is `not_found` (404).

schema.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.

parameters.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.
parameters.name: id

200.description: The contact with its new name.

delete.description: Deletes the contact and its opt-out links for good. Exception: for a contact that opted out, the server keeps the number (and nothing else) so that it cannot be added again; that record goes away with the account or when `sos_alerts` is withdrawn. Another user's contact is `not_found` (404).

schema.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.

parameters.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Create an opt-out link token for an invite SMS
post.description: Returns a new opt-out token for this contact, once. The app builds the link `<API address>/c#<token>` (the token in the URL FRAGMENT) and opens the SMS app with a prefilled invite that the user sends from their own phone. The server sends no message to a contact: no SMS, push or call. Earlier tokens of the contact stay valid. Errors: `contact_opted_out` (409); `rate_limited` (429) when the contact already has 10 links (no `Retry-After`) or the user created too many links today (with `Retry-After`). Then call `confirmContactInvite` when the user says the SMS was sent.

schema.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.

parameters.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Record that the user sent the invite SMS
post.description: Sets `invitedAt` to now. It records what the user said, not a delivery: the server cannot see the SMS. Safe to repeat. Errors (409): `contact_opted_out`; `conflict` when no invite link was created for the contact.

schema.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.

parameters.description: Id of the contact, as returned by the server.
parameters.name: id

get.summary: The opt-out page for emergency contacts
get.description: Public by design: a contact has no account. A static HTML page in English and Bengali, the same for everyone, with no cookie and no external resource. The link in the invite SMS is `/c#<token>`: a browser never sends the fragment to a server, so this request carries no token. The page sends the token in the body of `optOutContact` only when the visitor taps "Opt out". Not for the app.

post.summary: Opt out as an emergency contact
post.description: Public by design: called by the opt-out page with the token from the invite SMS, in the request body. The contact is then never alerted and cannot be invited or added again by that user. Safe to repeat (200 again). A malformed, unknown or no longer active token gets the same `not_found` (404). One rate limit is shared by all callers (`rate_limited`, 429, with `Retry-After`); nothing about the caller is stored or logged.

post.summary: Search for places by name, kind or brand
post.description: Forwards the search to a geocoding provider and returns matching places. **By name** (the default): with `nearLatitude`/`nearLongitude`, places near that point come first and each result carries `distanceMeters`; when too few are found nearby, places from further away follow. Without them, results are biased towards a default area. **By kind or brand**: when `category` is sent, or `q` is a word for a kind of place ("bank", "pharmacy") or a well-known brand, and the point is sent, only places inside a circle around the point are returned, nearest first, and the response says how wide the circle was (`searchedRadiusKm`). Such a search never adds places from outside the circle: an empty list means nothing of that kind is on the map there, which says nothing about whether one exists. The search travels in the request body, never in the URL, and is not stored or logged. Calling it again with the same body is safe (it changes nothing), so no `Idempotency-Key` is needed. Errors: `rate_limited` (429) and `search_unavailable` (503) may carry a `Retry-After` header in seconds; `search_not_configured` (503) means this instance has no geocoding key.

Returns the fastest route and up to two alternatives for walking or driving. The points travel in the request body, never in the URL, and neither they nor the routes are stored or logged. Calling it again with the same body is safe (it changes nothing), so no `Idempotency-Key` is needed. Routes carry no safety information.

Answers that are not failures of the service: `outside_covered_area` (422) when a point lies outside the area routes exist for; `route_too_long` (422) when the points are too far apart for the mode; `location_not_routable` (422) when a point is not near a road or path; `no_route_found` (404) when no way connects them.

`routing_unavailable` (503) comes with `Retry-After`. The routing service can be asleep: the first request after a quiet period may get this answer while it starts, and the same request succeeds a little later. The server makes one attempt and does not retry; the client does. `rate_limited` (429) also carries `Retry-After`. `routing_not_configured` (503) means this instance has no routing service.

200.description: One to three routes, fastest first.
